statement: Alphabet shares fell roughly 6% on the earnings day and other AI-infrastructure-adjacent names (Amazon, Oracle, Meta, Microsoft) also declined, suggesting investors treated the larger capex budget as a cost rather than a growth signal.
why: If equity markets start penalising rather than rewarding AI capex, the financing conditions facing the marginal buyer of compute tighten, which eventually feeds back into order books.

impact.mechanism: A negative share-price reaction to raised capex raises the cost of capital and board-level scrutiny for further AI build, which can slow the pace of incremental compute commitments even while current budgets rise.

evidence.source: Alphabet Investor Relations (press release dated 2026-07-22) via CNBC / MLQ News reporting
evidence.excerpt: Alphabet shares dropped roughly 6% after the earnings announcement

confidence.basis: Single-day market reaction reported by one secondary outlet; a one-session move is weak evidence of a durable financing-condition change.
